say.en: A new drip-irrigation method cuts a farmer's cost; a rise in diesel prices raises it. One shifts supply right, the other left. Then we add up all the firms. In this lesson: List determinants of a firm's supply curve.
Show the effect of a unit tax.
Derive the market supply curve.

title.en: Determinants of a firm's supply curve

body.en: A *firm's supply curve* is part of its marginal cost curve, so anything that changes marginal cost shifts it. (1) Technological progress lowers MC and shifts supply to the right. (2) A rise in input prices raises MC and shifts supply to the left. (3) A unit tax of ₹t raises MC by t at every output, shifting supply upward (left) by t. A change in the good's own price causes a movement along the supply curve.

points.en: Unit tax t → *supply* shifts up by t

narration.en: Better technology shifts supply right. Higher input prices or a unit tax shift supply left. The good's own price only moves us along the curve.
narration.kn: ಉತ್ತಮ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ ಪೂರೈಕೆಯನ್ನು ಬಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದಾನ ಬೆಲೆ ಏರಿಕೆ ಅಥವಾ ಘಟಕ ತೆರಿಗೆ ಎಡಕ್ಕೆ ಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸ್ವಂತ ಬೆಲೆ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ರೇಖೆಯ ಮೇಲೆ ಚಲನೆ ಮಾತ್ರ.

say.en: Better technology shifts supply right. Higher input prices or a unit tax shift supply left. The good's own price only moves us along the curve. Technology ↑ gives supply shifts right.

say.en: Input price ↑ gives supply shifts left.
Unit tax t gives supply shifts up by t.

title.en: Unit tax and adding up firms

say.en: A firm supplies along its MC: q equals p minus 10, so it starts supplying at 10 rupees.
A unit tax of 5 rupees raises marginal cost by 5 at every output. The supply curve shifts up by 5.
Market supply: firm 1 supplies p minus 10 from 10 rupees, firm 2 supplies p minus 15 from 15 rupees. Add quantities at each price.

title.en: From firm supply to market supply

caption.en: Firm 1 supplies p − 10 units at prices of ₹10 or more; firm 2 supplies p − 15 units at ₹15 or more. The market supply is their horizontal sum, so it bends at ₹15 where firm 2 joins. A rise in input costs shifts every supply curve up.
caption.kn: ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ 1 ₹10 ಅಥವಾ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಬೆಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ p − 10 ಘಟಕ; ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ 2 ₹15 ಅಥವಾ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನಲ್ಲಿ p − 15 ಘಟಕ ಪೂರೈಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ ಪೂರೈಕೆ ಅವುಗಳ ಅಡ್ಡ ಮೊತ್ತ. ಆದಾನ ವೆಚ್ಚ ಏರಿದರೆ ಪೂರೈಕೆ ಮೇಲೆ ಸರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: From firm supply to market supply Firm 1 supplies p minus 10 units at prices of 10 rupees or more; firm 2 supplies p minus 15 units at 15 rupees or more. The market supply is their horizontal sum, so it bends at 15 rupees where firm 2 joins. A rise in input costs shifts every supply curve up.
say.kn: ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ 1 10 rupees ಅಥವಾ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಬೆಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ p minus 10 ಘಟಕ; ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ 2 15 rupees ಅಥವಾ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನಲ್ಲಿ p minus 15 ಘಟಕ ಪೂರೈಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ ಪೂರೈಕೆ ಅವುಗಳ ಅಡ್ಡ ಮೊತ್ತ. ಆದಾನ ವೆಚ್ಚ ಏರಿದರೆ ಪೂರೈಕೆ ಮೇಲೆ ಸರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: The *market supply curve* shows the total quantity all firms together offer at each price. It is the horizontal sum of the individual firms' supply curves. If firm 1 supplies $s_1 = p - 10$ for $p \ge 10$ and firm 2 supplies $s_2 = p - 15$ for $p \ge 15$, market supply is 0 for p < 10, $p - 10$ for $10 \le p < 15$ and $2p - 25$ for $p \ge 15$. With n identical firms each supplying s(p), market supply is n × s(p).

points.en: *Market supply* = Σ firm supplies at each price
n identical firms: S = n × s(p)

narration.en: Market supply is the horizontal sum of all firms' supply curves: at each price, add up what every firm offers.
narration.kn: ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ ಪೂರೈಕೆ ಎಲ್ಲ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗಳ ಪೂರೈಕೆ ರೇಖೆಗಳ ಅಡ್ಡ ಮೊತ್ತ: ಪ್ರತಿ ಬೆಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆ ನೀಡುವುದನ್ನು ಕೂಡಿಸಿ.

problem.en: Firm 1 supplies s₁ = p − 10 for p ≥ 10 (zero below), and firm 2 supplies s₂ = p − 15 for p ≥ 15 (zero below). Find market supply at prices ₹8, ₹12 and ₹20.

steps.en: p = 8: both firms supply 0; market supply = 0.

answer.en: Market supply = 0, 2 and 15 units at ₹8, ₹12 and ₹20.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Firm 1 supplies s₁ = p − 10 for p ≥ 10 (zero below), and firm 2 supplies s₂ = p − 15 for p ≥ 15 (zero below). Find market supply at prices ₹8, ₹12 and ₹20.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Firm 1 supplies s 1 equals p minus 10 for p is greater than or equal to 10 zero below, and firm 2 supplies s 2 equals p minus 15 for p is greater than or equal to 15 zero below. Find market supply at prices 8, rupees 12 rupees and 20 rupees.
p equals 8: both firms supply 0; market supply equals 0.
p equals 12: s 1 equals 2, s 2 equals 0; market supply equals 2.
p equals 20: s 1 equals 10, s 2 equals 5; market supply equals 15 (check: 2 times 20 minus 25 equals 15).
So the answer is Market supply equals 0, 2 and 15 units at 8, rupees 12 rupees and 20 rupees.
